title: Traffic-slope failover scheduler and KV sanity harness
creator: Aisha Raman
description:
Introduce an automated traffic-slope failover scheduler and a KV sanity harness to run controlled active->passive drills. Goal: provide a safe, observable way to shift production traffic incrementally to a passive region while validating state consistency, preserving SLOs, and enabling automatic rollback when safety gates fail.

Background: Current DR drills are noisy (big switchover waves) and require manual pacing to avoid mass circuit breaker trips and customer-visible latency spikes. We need a system that progressively shifts traffic according to a configurable slope, ties into circuit-breaker and load-shedding controls, and runs a KV snapshot/compare harness to assert read-after-write and snapshot integrity across regions.

Scope: scheduler service, integration with routing and RBAC, observable dashboards, KV sanity harness that can perform dry-run snapshot comparisons and targeted key probes. Includes runbook updates and scheduled drill automation.

Non-goals: full cross-region state sync tooling (we assume snapshots produced by backup pipeline), user-facing UI for scheduling (CLI/API only for first iteration).
acceptance_criteria: Scheduler can execute a multi-step traffic slope according to a JSON specification (percent increments, hold durations)
During a scheduled drill, routing telemetry shows traffic shifting per the schedule with <5% deviation from configured slope
KV sanity harness runs pre-promote snapshot checks and targeted read-after-write probes; finds <0.1% key divergence for synthetic test dataset
Automatic rollback triggers if latency SLO (P50 < 60ms, P95 < 220ms) or error-rate SLO (>0.5%) violate for >2 consecutive slope steps
Runbook produced and exercised in two internal drills; postmortem checklist added to console runbooks page
End-to-end test available in CI that can simulate a small-scale slope and assert circuit-breaker interactions
steps: Design: finalize slope spec (steps, percent, hold_ms, abort_conditions) and publish design doc
Infra: provision scheduler service (k8s deployment), RBAC and service-account for routing control
Routing integration: expose scheduler hooks in smart-routing to apply per-tenant traffic weights; implement idempotent apply and rollback APIs
KV harness: implement snapshot-compare utility that pulls snapshot manifests, computes key hash batches, and reports divergence with reason codes
SLO guards: wire latency/error metrics to scheduler abort conditions; implement cooldown/backoff on partial failures
DR runbook: author step-by-step checklist, pre-flight checks, and operator rollback commands
Canary: run internal canary on dev region (10% traffic slope) + run KV harness against synthetic dataset
Validation: run scheduled full drill on staging and capture metrics, perform postmortem and adjust abort thresholds
Scheduled production drill: announce to stakeholders, execute under oncall supervision, and validate rollback behavior
